deviation_from_approved_design.not_verified_by_substitution: nothing in the audit relies on the runtime's identity; every check is an observation from inside the subject.

audit_integrity.missing_binary_never_counted_as_blocked: every client was verified PRESENT in-container before its check; curl, wget, git, npm, node, python3, dig, nc are all installed deliberately
audit_integrity.unexplained_timeout_never_counted_as_blo: no check resolved as INCONCLUSIVE_TIMEOUT; every block carries an explicit errno or proxy status
audit_integrity.control_comparison: an identical container from the same image, differing ONLY in network attachment (v4-egress-net instead of v4-subject-net), ran the identical script. Every blocked check REACHED its target in the control.
audit_integrity.alternate_interface_check: subject has exactly lo and eth0 (10.83.0.2/24); no default route; 172.18.0.1, 172.18.0.2, 192.168.5.1, 192.168.5.2 all ENETUNREACH
audit_integrity.ipv6_check: no IPv6 route in the subject; IPv6 literal connect is ENETUNREACH. Recorded as PASS_UNATTRIBUTABLE: the control container is also IPv6-less, so this VM provides no IPv6 anywhere. IPv6 offers no bypass, but the block cannot be attributed to the internal-network design.
audit_integrity.dns_check: subject's embedded resolver returns SERVFAIL for external names; dig TXT returns nothing. The control resolves github.com and retrieves real TXT records, so the subject's DNS failure is attributable to network attachment. No DNS data channel.
audit_integrity.subject_error_output_preserved: logs/audit-subject.jsonl (raw exit codes and output for every check)

bypass_found_and_closed_during_audit.finding: the Colima VM's sshd listens on the subject bridge gateway 10.83.0.1 and tcp/22 was OPEN from inside the subject container
bypass_found_and_closed_during_audit.why_it_matters: a shell on the VM is a host with full internet; this is a pivot the design did not anticipate
bypass_found_and_closed_during_audit.closure: iptables -I INPUT -i br-<subject-net> -j DROP inside the VM. Container-to-container traffic on that bridge does not traverse INPUT, so subject -> proxy is unaffected.
bypass_found_and_closed_during_audit.verified_after: 10.83.0.1 tcp/22, 53, 2375, 3128 all closed/filtered from the subject; proxy:3128 still OPEN; inference still 3/3; full network audit re-run with 0 failures
bypass_found_and_closed_during_audit.persistence: re-applied idempotently by net-up.sh; must be re-asserted after any colima restart

hostname_allowlist_decision.models_opencode_ai: attempted 7 times and DENIED every time, yet inference succeeded 4/4. The frozen rule permits adding a hostname only if inference FAILS without it. It did not fail, so models.opencode.ai was NOT added.
hostname_allowlist_decision.mcp_exa_ai: opencode ships a built-in Exa web-search tool that addresses mcp.exa.ai. Denied. It must never be added to the allowlist -- it is a general web-retrieval channel.

residual_limitations: The model provider itself is not isolated: these are public express/fastify/hapi bugs and the model's training data may contain the historical fixes. Inherent to the corpus choice; recorded, not solved.
IPv6 blocking is not attributable to the design, only to this VM having no IPv6 at all.

The allowlist was validated against 4 inference runs of a trivial prompt. A long repair run may exercise additional hostnames; any such attempt will appear in the squid deny log and must be evaluated under the frozen rule rather than pre-approved.
Host free disk fell from 6.9 GB to ~2 GB during setup. Probe runs should re-check headroom before starting.
